content.text: Intent

A small school register: schools and the students enrolled in them. A school holds its name, location and ranking; a student holds a name, a class and an age, and points at the school they attend. Serves anyone who needs to browse schools and their students — the platform's standard screens cover create, edit, browse and delete for both.
Scope
IN: a School entity (name, location, ranking) and a Student entity (name, class, age, school reference).
IN: a Student's school reference must point at a real school.
OUT: enrolment history, transfers between schools, grades/subjects, teachers, anything beyond the two entities' plain fields.
Scenarios
None — the entities' standard screens cover create, edit, browse and delete; no ordered process is requested.
Requirements
None — every rule is carried by the bean tables (required fields, the Student→School reference, the ranking bounds).
Data model
bean: School
bean: Student

cells.text: the class the student is in, e.g. "7B"

content.text: Relationships: a Student belongs to exactly one School; a School has many Students.
User interface

The beans' standard search screens and edit forms. The author asked for a colourful, clean, friendly look: both beans' default forms carry it — a themed header (gradient avatar, title, soft chip), colour-coded section labels with accent dots, and rounded bordered sections — all through theme palette slots, so it stays clean in light and dark mode. Ranking shows a helper hint ("1 is the best").
Dependencies
None — this spec relies on no other spec, no existing entity and no external system.
Constraints
Considered, none apply beyond the platform's own rules: authorization (any signed-in user, platform default), performance, volume, availability, audit, privacy, locale, cost.
Acceptance criteria
None — the platform's generated tests cover the table rules (required fields, reference integrity, min/max bounds).
Migration & compatibility
None — new entities, nothing to migrate.
Artifacts
A School entity and a Student entity, each with its standard search screen and edit form.
